title: LIV Golf Files for Chapter 11 Bankruptcy With BC Partners Restructuring Agreement
dek: LIV Golf filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in New Jersey on September 8, 2026, with BC Partners Credit as its proposed new investor under a restructuring support agreement. The filing reveals $500 million to $1 billion in liabilities against $100 million to $500 million in assets, with at least $45 million in unpaid player compensation.
author: The GoCheckMySports Desk
key_fact: LIV Golf filed Chapter 11 bankruptcy on September 8, 2026, with BC Partners Credit backing a restructuring aimed at creating a player-majority-owned league in 2027.
bottom_line: The BC Partners restructuring deal has not closed and requires court approval, leaving the timeline and terms of LIV's next phase unconfirmed. The gap between the $49.6 million in available financing and the $500 million to $1 billion in estimated liabilities determines what fraction of player and vendor claims can be satisfied. Whether the 75-player, lower-purse model proposed for 2027 will attract sufficient player participation remains unresolved.
body:
LIV Golf filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in the U.S. Bankruptcy Court of New Jersey on Tuesday, September 8, 2026, according to reporting by CBS Sports and Front Office Sports. The filing came alongside an announcement of a restructuring support agreement with BC Partners Credit, the London and New York-based investment firm exploring a recapitalization transaction with the league.
LIV's bankruptcy petition estimates liabilities between $500 million and $1 billion against assets valued at $100 million to $500 million. The Saudi Public Investment Fund (PIF), which ended its funding in April 2026 after more than five years of investment, has committed $49.6 million in debtor-in-possession financing to fund operations during the court-supervised restructuring. That financing covers less than 10 percent of LIV's estimated liabilities, according to reporting.
The unsecured player creditors list is led by , followed by Bryson DeChambeau and Dustin Johnson, each with claims exceeding $5 million.  Front Office Sports reports that vendor IMG Media is owed the largest single amount among non-player creditors at $3.2 million. GSE Worldwide, DeChambeau's agency, is listed for $1.28 million. Golf influencer Rich Shiels is owed $1.39 million, the state of Louisiana $1.22 million, and Fresh Tape Media $1.2 million. Rahm is separately reported to be owed more than $100 million from his multiyear contract signed before the 2024 season, an amount far exceeding the current Q3 2026 payables listed in court filings.
LIV Golf was forced to cancel two tournaments and failed to pay vendors and some players after the PIF ended funding, according to court documents obtained by the Financial Times and cited by CBS Sports. The league intends to resume competition in 2027 under a new player-majority ownership model, with field sizes expanding to 75 players per event, Monday qualifiers introduced as a new pathway, and a cut implemented for the first time. According to Front Office Sports, LIV plans events across five continents including Australia, South Africa, Mexico, England, Hong Kong, and the United States, though no definitive 2027 schedule or individual event decisions have been announced.
Gene Davis, chairman of an independent board of directors established after PIF's exit, stated per Front Office Sports that the board "reviewed all available options and believe today's actions reflect the most responsible path forward for the League and its stakeholders." LIV CEO Scott O'Neil said: "This process gives us the structure and time to pursue a landmark transaction and begin the next chapter of LIV Golf," and noted by way of example that companies including Marvel Entertainment, Delta Airlines, Caesars Entertainment, the Los Angeles Dodgers, Pittsburgh Penguins, and Leeds United F.C. have taken similar Chapter 11 paths.
BBC Sport reports that contracts under the previous LIV Golf iteration will terminate because of the court filing, with amounts owed to players and creditors addressed through the court process. No obligation exists for players to sign with a restructured LIV 2.0 regardless of previous multi-year agreements. CBS Sports reports that it remains unclear when players would be able to enter discussions with other tours, and that the PGA Tour has been hesitant to open an additional pathway for remaining LIV players to return.
Rahm, speaking to BBC Sport on Tuesday, said: "There's just a lot of things in place, right. There's a lot of things that could happen and it's one of those things where time's gonna tell... I still have a contract with LIV 1.0 that I'm more than willing to fulfill." LIV's proposed transaction with BC Partners remains subject to court and stakeholder approval.
